extracted.intended_audience: NIH R01 applicants (PIs/co-investigators), institutional grants administrators, and NIH reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and reviewer critique guidance for evaluating an NIH R01 resubmission/renewal, including the five core review criteria, additional review elements (human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, authentication of resources), and budget/administrative recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: summary judgment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. The overall impact reflects the committee's collective enthusiasm; reviewers' individual overall scores are averaged to produce the impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance — assessment of whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate importance of the problem, potential to improve scientific knowledge or clinical practice, and generalizability/translation to other systems (e.g., translation to other Gram+ pathogens noted as a major strength). Strengths and weaknesses should be documented (e.g., 'None noted' when appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) — evaluation of the PI(s) and key personnel's qualifications, leadership, and track record to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prior productivity, complementary expertise among team members, prior work in the field (e.g., discovery history), and potential risks (e.g., loss of proximity between collaborators). Strengths and moderate/major designations can be used to communicate impact on the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation — whether the project challenges current paradigms, addresses an innovative hypothesis, or uses novel concepts, approaches, or technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty of concepts, methods, and potential to shift existing paradigms. Note any contrary evidence (e.g., existence of prior small-molecule virulence inhibitors) and whether claimed innovations are genuinely new vs incremental. Examples and specific innovative methods (e.g., nanodiscs, novel assays) are cited as strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach — evaluation of the overall strategy, methodology, analyses, and feasibility including consideration of preliminary data, controls, alternatives, and contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge rigor and feasibility: clarity of methods, sufficiency of preliminary data, presence of proper controls, acknowledgement of alternative explanations, and contingency plans. Specific technical risks (e.g., difficulty solving membrane protein X-ray structure) should be identified as weaknesses (major/moderate/minor). Removal or inappropriate inclusion of study elements (e.g., animal studies) may be flagged as unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment — assessment of institutional support, equipment, facilities, and whether the scientific environment contributes to the probability of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional strengths, collaborations, and resource availability. Note potential logistical issues (e.g., collaborators located at distant institutions) as potential weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for Human Subjects — determination of applicability and adequacy of protections when human subjects are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no human subjects are involved, mark Not Applicable. When applicable, reviewers assess human subjects protections; absence or inadequate description results in concerns. Explicit statement required in application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals — evaluation of whether vertebrate animals are involved and, if so, whether the application addresses required points for their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no vertebrate animals are proposed, mark Not Applicable. If a vertebrate animal section is included without proposing animal work, reviewers may flag this as inappropriate (Unacceptable) and recommend budget adjustments. When animals are proposed, reviewers expect the section to address the required four points and assess appropriateness, welfare, and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards / Biosafety
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazards — assessment of biosafety considerations for proposed work involving pathogenic organisms, hazardous agents, or other biohazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications proposing work with pathogens must explicitly describe biosafety procedures and facility approvals (e.g., BSL2). Lack of biosafety discussion can be judged 'Unacceptable' even if investigators have prior experience. Reviewers will cite missing biosafety details as a substantive weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources — applicants must include a PDF attachment describing plans for authentication per NOT-OD-16-011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2016 are required to include an attachment describing plans for authentication of key resources. Reviewers were asked to consider information provided in this attachment as part of their evaluation; missing attachments mean the item 'could not be assessed' and may be judged Unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (Amended Application) Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission — reviewers assess how the applicant addressed criticisms from prior reviews and whether revisions adequately resolve earlier concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit responses to prior critiques, removal or addition of experiments (e.g., removal of animal studies), new preliminary data supporting feasibility, and whether remaining concerns have been addressed. Reviewers note if prior concerns were 'adequately addressed' or if issues remain (especially in specific aims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal — for renewal applications, reviewers evaluate productivity during the prior funding period and whether the progress supports continued funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess publications and tangible outputs from previous support, whether aims have been achieved or advanced, and the appropriateness of proposed future work in light of prior productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and Period of Support — assessment of budget items relative to proposed work and committee recommendations to modify budget if requested items are not part of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative note: the budget shown is the requested budget and may be adjusted by grants management based on committee recommendations. Reviewers may recommend budget reductions for items inconsistent with the research plan (e.g., funds requested for animal work that is not proposed). Flag possible overlap and recommend specific modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Mechanics and Review Process Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring mechanics — criterion scores (1-9) are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers; overall impact scores are averaged and multiplied by 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are entered by individual reviewers before the meeting and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score directly during discussion. The impact score is computed from averaged overall scores. Percentile rankings may also be provided.
